job.title: Member Services and Advocacy Lead (Lived Experience Identified)
job.description:
Membership and Advocacy Lead (Lived Experience Identified)

Help build Australia’s first national peer-led membership body for mental health and suicide prevention peer workers – from wherever you are.

Why you’ll love this role

  • Shape a brand-new national organisation at a critical moment for Australia’s peer workforce.
  • Lead with your lived experience – and see it embedded in everything AAPW does.
  • Work remotely from anywhere in Australia, with some domestic travel to connect with members.
  • Competitive package: SCHADS 7.1 – $124,000 plus super and salary packaging.

About the Australian Association of Peer Workers (AAPW) AAPW is a peer-led professional membership body for mental health and suicide prevention peer workers. It is a national entity, auspiced by the National Mental Health Consumer Alliance, in partnership with the Indigenous Australian Lived Experience Centre and Mental Health Carers Australia. Its purpose is simple: to strengthen, support and advocate for the peer workforce across Australia.

The role As Membership and Advocacy Lead, you will lead AAPW’s communications, engagement and member experience. You’ll drive initiatives that attract, support and grow a strong national membership, and make sure members feel connected, informed and represented.

You’ll oversee AAPW’s public voice across digital and sector platforms, coordinate member services and events, and make sure peer workers have meaningful opportunities for connection, advice and support. You’ll gather insights from members and the wider peer workforce to shape AAPW’s priorities, advocacy and strategic direction, and lead jurisdictional and national co-design so lived experience voices are embedded in every initiative.
What you’ll do

  • Manage day-to-day communications and engagement, including digital content, newsletters, social media, surveys, campaigns and stakeholder communications.
  • Design, oversee and continuously improve Member Services.
  • Plan and deliver member forums, events and engagement activities that strengthen connection and participation.
  • Lead member-informed advocacy, including policy submissions, position papers, consultation responses and sector campaigns.

What you’ll bring

  • Tertiary qualifications in a relevant field (communications, peer work, community development, social science, public health or public policy) and/or equivalent experience.
  • At least three years’ experience in a designated Lived Experience role (peer work, leadership, policy, project, academic, First Nations, consumer, carer or suicide prevention).
  • Experience in a communications role, including leading communication strategy development and delivery across newsletters, social media, campaigns, websites and stakeholder channels.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparing submissions, reports and public-facing content.
  • Experience contributing to advocacy, policy development, consultations or sector reform related to peer work or lived experience leadership.
  • The ability to engage members, the peer workforce and the broader community to support membership growth.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake regular interstate travel, and a reliable internet connection and work-from-home resources, as this is a national, virtual workplace.

Designated Lived Experience role

We’re looking for someone with personal or carer lived experience of mental health challenges and recovery, and/or lived experience of suicidality or suicide, who has drawn on that experience in meaningful ways to support others, lead change and influence systems.

This is a genuine occupational requirement under relevant anti-discrimination legislation across Australia, including section 66(s)(c) of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (WA).

Not sure whether your experience fits? We’d love to hear from you – reach out for a confidential conversation. Beaumont People uses a trauma-informed recruitment approach: you will not be asked to disclose personal details of your experiences. A simple self-declaration confirms eligibility, with optional opportunities to reflect on how lived experience informs your leadership practice.

How to apply There are two steps, and both are required:

  1. Submit your resume. Click apply through the advertisement on the Beaumont People website, SEEK or any of our other advertisements, and upload your resume and any supporting documents.
  2. Complete the Expression of Interest (EOI) form. Submit it online at https://forms.office.com/r/SckjYKUWYU. If the link doesn’t open directly, copy and paste it into your web browser.

There is no closing date. Applications are reviewed as they are received, so apply soon. Questions? Contact Rhonda at rhonda@beaumontpeople.com.au. Beaumont People is exclusively partnering with AAPW on this recruitment, so please direct all enquiries to Rhonda.

Join us in making a difference – be part of AAPW.
Our commitment to you At Beaumont People, we’re committed to a recruitment experience where people feel welcomed, respected and supported. We value diverse perspectives and life experiences, and we focus on what you can bring, not where you come from or how your journey has unfolded.
We’re mindful of the barriers faced by people from marginalised or underrepresented communities, and we are intentional about creating fair, accessible and inclusive processes. The Organisation

The National Mental Health Consumer Alliance (Alliance) believes people with lived and living experience must shape the decisions that affect their lives.

Australia's national peak body for mental health consumers, the Alliance is a federation of state and territory consumer peaks, led by and for people with lived and living experience. The Candidate Profile

The Alliance is seeking a collaborative Chair who connects people around a shared purpose, builds trust and alignment through influence, and develops an open, honest partnership with the CEO, while maintaining the important distinction between governance and operational leadership.

The ideal candidate will bring Board experience and sound governance knowledge, with Chair experience highly regarded but not essential. Experience in a federated, membership-based peak body or similarly complex environment, financial literacy and skilled facilitation will be valued. Formal governance qualifications are not required.

Personal lived or living experience of mental health challenges as a consumer (rather than as a carer or supporter) is essential. We define consumer lived experience as mental health challenges that have caused life as we knew it to change so significantly, we have had to reimagine and redefine ourselves, our place in the world and our future plans. The successful candidate will have drawn on that experience in a meaningful way to support others, lead change and influence systems. They will be guided by lived experience values and committed to amplifying consumer and survivor voices in national reform. We recognise lived experience as a form of leadership and expertise, and are committed to a safe, inclusive, respectful, accessible and trauma-informed recruitment process.
